statement: The Teutonic Order's Baltic state transformed from a crusading military order-state into a secular duchy when Grand Master Albert of Hohenzollern-Ansbach (1511–1525) converted to Lutheranism on Martin Luther's advice (1525) and secularized the remaining Ducal Prussia as a hereditary Hohenzollern duchy under Polish suzerainty. The transformation was theologically radical — the first major application of Lutheranism to state reorganization — and politically significant: the Hohenzollern Duchy of Prussia became the nucleus of the future Kingdom of Prussia that eventually unified Germany.
